newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank loans seen falling 1% in 2nd half - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank loans seen falling 1% in 2nd half - paper.

text.p: Outstanding loans of Japanese banks are expected to fall in the six months to next March 31 by about one percent from the same period last year, marking the first year-on-year decline, a business daily said on Friday.
Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the expected fall could slow the Japanese economy.

Although some major banks expect their lending in the half-year period to grow by less than one percent, many see their lending staying at the same level or falling one to two percent compared with the same period a year ago, it said.

An overall fall is expected because slow demand for borrowing, especially from large companies, is expected to continue and also because banks are trying to recover non-performing loans in the half-year period, it said.
